page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-2 is a memory-oriented virtual machine configuration within the compute-optimized C2D family. The instance is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, supplying 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped across a single physical core with simultaneous multithreading. It includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity is provisioned at 16.0 GB, establishing a high allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. No local storage is bundled with the instance, requiring reliance on remote persistent volumes, and no dedicated GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

In synthetic benchmarks, the instance demonstrates distinct single-thread and multi-thread characteristics. Single-core evaluation via stress-ng registers a strong result of 2923.78, placing it in the upper quartile. Conversely, multi-core throughput remains restricted by the physical single-core footprint, scoring 2929.68 in stress-ng and 2038.0 in Geekbench multi-core tests, both placing in the bottom 25%. Instruction-level evaluations reflect standard Zen 3 capabilities with support for AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, though vector performance without AVX-512 keeps extended instruction metrics in lower percentiles. Memory bandwidth benchmarks yield 34.65 GB/sec for uncached 256MB reads and 24.29 GB/sec for writes. Application-specific tests show average text processing and compression metrics, such as 28.16 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip, while parallel workloads like Clang compilation and static web serving throughput sit in lower tiers due to overall thread limits.

From an efficiency standpoint, the c2d-highmem-2 offers an economical path for workloads that require substantial memory per thread without the expense of scaling out vCPU counts. Because multi-core capacity is limited to two virtual threads on one physical core, the configuration presents a throughput tradeoff in parallel compute. The instance is primarily matched for small in-memory caches, lightweight database services, single-threaded backend services, staging environments, and intermediate ETL tasks that benefit from 16 GB of RAM but do not require heavy parallel execution.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-2 is an x86_64 virtual machine featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs across 1 physical core of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, complemented by 16.0 GB of system memory. Lacking local disk storage and hardware GPU acceleration, it relies on network storage solutions. Hardware evaluations reveal strong single-core compute performance, as reflected in high stress-ng single-threaded marks, balanced against moderate multi-core throughput given the single physical core architecture. Memory bandwidth scales to 34.65 GB/sec read and 24.29 GB/sec write on uncached blocks. The machine profile provides an elevated 8 GB per vCPU ratio, offering resource efficiency for applications requiring substantial memory without paying for excessive processor cores. The c2d-highmem-2 is best suited for memory-intensive entry-level workloads, including smaller in-memory data stores, background task runners, single-threaded processing queues, and lightweight database instances.
